ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $A$, $B$, and $D$ are consecutively on the same straight line, $\angle A=\angle D=\angle CBE=90^\circ$, $AC=BD$, $CB=BE$. If $AC=2$ and $AD=6$, what is the length of $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $AC=BD=2$ and $AD=6$,\\
then $AB=AD-BD=6-2=4$,\\
thus $CB^{2}=AC^{2}+AB^{2}=2^{2}+4^{2}=20$,\\
which means $CB^{2}=BE^{2}=20$,\\
therefore $CE= \sqrt{CB^{2}+BE^{2}}=\sqrt{20+20}=2\sqrt{10}$,\\
hence the length of $CE$ is $CE=\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}$.
